summary:
We created a health monitoring software which aims to maximize the use of existing technology in-use by space agencies to provide useful guidance while remaining medically accurate.
The novelty lies in accepting categorical data, not only data measured from sensors, as the feelings of the astronauts themselves is vital to proper diagnosis.
We also found women's health and mental health to be disregarded in a lot of health monitoring systems, so we implemented proper data collection for this as well.
details:
The tech stack is InfluxDB which stores the data from the sensors (including the sleep sensors and ActiWatch Spectrum) and categorical data, the data that the astronauts report to the monitoring system on a regular basis.

The system is built on the assumption that a computer cannot fully diagnose an astronaut's condition solely from the limited data provided to it; instead, we've designed a system that only tries to enhance the crew members' understanding of their own health, without giving them misinformation. In the case the medical officer is unavailable the software gives a diagnosis on a best-effort basis.

The UI is designed to be the most convenient for the astronauts, with the important info placed at the centre, with an emergency causing a highly visible ALERT with the problem instantly visible to the astronauts.
projectRefs: Medically induced amenorrhea in female astronauts
